title: Are unlimited approvals dangerous?
seoTitle: Are Unlimited Token Approvals Dangerous? | CRYPY
description: Unlimited approvals save fees but cover every token of that kind you will ever hold. Learn when they are risky, how Permit2 differs, and when to limit them.
summary: Why "unlimited" also covers tokens you receive later, and when it's worth limiting.
inShort: An unlimited approval covers every token of that kind in your wallet, now and later.
It is only as safe as the contract you gave it to.
Limit or revoke approvals for apps you don't use often.

blocks.text: When you approve a token, the app chooses the amount. Many choose the largest number possible, so you never have to approve again. Your wallet may show it as "unlimited" or as a very long number.
The approval doesn't move anything by itself. It means the spender contract may move any amount of that token from your wallet, at any time, without asking you again.

items: **The contract is hacked.** Attackers can use existing approvals to drain wallets that approved it.
**The contract was malicious.** A scam site's "claim" button can be an approval for the scammer's contract.
**You forgot about it.** An approval from years ago still works today, for tokens you received since.

blocks.text: A limited approval caps the damage at the amount you approved. An unlimited one doesn't.
Some apps, including Uniswap and PancakeSwap, use **Permit2**: you approve the Permit2 contract once per token, then sign separate permissions for each app, with an amount and an expiry date.
Check both levels: the approval to Permit2 itself, and the app permissions inside it. The [Approval Checker](tool:approval-checker) reads both and shows when each Permit2 permission expires.
NFT collections have a wider permission that covers every NFT you hold in the collection. It is common on marketplaces, and a frequent target of phishing. Treat it like an unlimited token approval.

items: When your wallet lets you, edit the amount to what you plan to use.
Revoke approvals for apps you no longer use, especially on tokens worth a lot.
Keep large holdings in a wallet you don't use to try new apps.
Check your approvals now and then with the [Approval Checker](tool:approval-checker).

faq.q: Should I revoke every unlimited approval?
faq.a: Not necessarily. For a well-known app you use often, revoking means approving again (and paying a fee) next time. Focus on apps you no longer use and contracts you don't recognize.
Safer, because the spender can move at most that amount. It is still a permission: revoke it if you don't need it.

faq.q: Why does my wallet show a huge number instead of "unlimited"?
faq.a: "Unlimited" is just the largest number the token's contract can store. Wallets show it in different ways.
